title: Integral Weyl atlas on the schematic closure of an admissible representation
statement:
Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional rational vector space and $R\subset V\setminus\{0\}$ a reduced crystallographic root system spanning $V$, with coroot functionals $c_\alpha$ and weight lattice $P=\{v\in V:c_\alpha(v)\in\mathbf Z\text{ for all }\alpha\in R\}$ as in [lem-sfb-root-datum-lattice-embedding]. Fix a base $\Delta$, so every root has integral coordinates in $\Delta$ all of one sign. Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional split semisimple rational Lie algebra [def-wf-lie-algebra, def-wf-semisimple-lie-algebra] with splitting Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$ and Chevalley basis $h_\delta,e_\alpha$ in the conventions of [lem-sfb-chevalley-admissible-representation]. Thus $\mathfrak h^\vee=V$, $h_\alpha=c_\alpha$, $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak h\oplus\bigoplus_{\alpha\in R}\mathbf Qe_\alpha$, $[h,e_\alpha]=\alpha(h)e_\alpha$, $[e_\alpha,e_{-\alpha}]=h_\alpha$, and $[e_\alpha,e_\beta]=\pm(p_{\alpha,\beta}+1)e_{\alpha+\beta}$ if the sum is a root and is zero if the sum is neither a root nor zero, where $p_{\alpha,\beta}=\max\{p\geq0:\beta-p\alpha\in R\}$. Let $\rho:\mathfrak g\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathbf Q}(W)$ be a faithful Lie representation, with $W$ finite-dimensional, weight decomposition $W=\bigoplus_{\lambda\in\Omega}W_\lambda$ with $W_\lambda\ne0$ and $\rho(h)w=\lambda(h)w$ on $W_\lambda$, finite $\Omega\subset P$ and $\mathbf Z\Omega=P$. Let $\Lambda\subset W$ be a finite free $\mathbf Z$-lattice with $\Lambda\otimes\mathbf Q=W$, such that $\Lambda=\bigoplus_{\lambda\in\Omega}(\Lambda\cap W_\lambda)$. Assume every $\rho(e_\alpha)$ is nilpotent and every $D_{\alpha,m}=\rho(e_\alpha)^m/m!$ preserves $\Lambda$.

For any commutative ring $A$, write $\operatorname{GL}_\Lambda(A)=\operatorname{Aut}_A(\Lambda\otimes_{\mathbf Z}A)$; this is the affine $\mathbf Z$-scheme with matrix coordinates and inverse determinant. Set $\mathcal T=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[P]$, where $\mathbf Z[P]$ has basis $e^\lambda$, product $e^\lambda e^\mu=e^{\lambda+\mu}$ and Hopf maps $e^\lambda\mapsto e^\lambda\otimes e^\lambda$, $e^\lambda\mapsto1$, $e^\lambda\mapsto e^{-\lambda}$. Map $\mathcal T$ to $\operatorname{GL}_\Lambda$ by the character $\lambda$ on each weight summand. Define polynomial matrix maps $y_\alpha:\mathbf A^1_{\mathbf Z}\to\operatorname{GL}_\Lambda$ by $y_\alpha(a)=\sum_{m\geq0}D_{\alpha,m}a^m$. Let $H_{\mathbf Q}$ be the smallest closed subgroup of $\operatorname{GL}_{W}$ containing $\mathcal T_{\mathbf Q}$ and all $(y_\alpha)_{\mathbf Q}$. Define its schematic closure by
$$I=\ker\bigl(\mathbf Z[\operatorname{GL}_\Lambda]\longrightarrow\mathbf Q[H_{\mathbf Q}]\bigr),\qquad \mathcal C=\operatorname{Spec}\bigl(\mathbf Z[\operatorname{GL}_\Lambda]/I\bigr).$$
Group schemes over $\mathbf Z$ have multiplication, identity and inverse satisfying the group diagrams of [def-sc-group-scheme], with base $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$.

Let $R^+$ be the roots with nonnegative simple-root coefficients, $N=|R^+|$, and enumerate $R^+$ in an order refining nondecreasing height, the sum of the simple-root coefficients. Put $p_\pm(a)=\prod_{\beta\in R^+}y_{\pm\beta}(a_\beta)$ in that order. Let $W_R$ be the finite reflection group generated by $s_\delta(v)=v-c_\delta(v)\delta$, $\delta\in\Delta$. For each $w\in W_R$ choose a reduced expression $w=s_{\delta_1}\cdots s_{\delta_l}$ and put
$$n_w=\prod_{j=1}^l\bigl(y_{\delta_j}(1)y_{-\delta_j}(-1)y_{\delta_j}(1)\bigr)\in\operatorname{GL}_\Lambda(\mathbf Z),\qquad n_1=1.$$
Then $\mathcal C$ is an affine group scheme over $\mathbf Z$ with the induced matrix group operations, and the maps
$$\theta_w:\mathbf A_{\mathbf Z}^{N}\times\mathcal T\times\mathbf A_{\mathbf Z}^{N}\longrightarrow\mathcal C,\qquad(a,t,b)\longmapsto n_wp_-(a)t p_+(b)$$
are open immersions whose images cover $\mathcal C$. Here an open immersion identifies its source with an open subscheme, as in [def-weil-open-immersion]. The assertion includes $R=\varnothing$, when $V=P=0$, $\mathcal C=1$ and $\theta_1$ is the identity of $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$.

source.place: Section 23h, equation (153), printed p.510, and Reductive groups over Z, printed p.511. Agent-stated integral atlas input to the Chevalley construction; this atlas is not proved in the field-only Theorem 23.72. WANTED: Steinberg, Lectures on Chevalley Groups (1967), integral Chevalley construction and big-cell/Bruhat charts over Z.

proof.text: Put $B=\mathbf Z[\operatorname{GL}_\Lambda]/I$. It embeds in $\mathbf Q[H_{\mathbf Q}]$, so is torsion-free over $\mathbf Z$. Both $B$ and the rational vector space $\mathbf Q[H_{\mathbf Q}]$ are flat by [lem-weil-pbc-pid-torsion-free-module-flat]. Applying [lem-trf-flat-tensor-preserves-injection] twice to $B\hookrightarrow\mathbf Q[H_{\mathbf Q}]$ embeds $B\otimes_{\mathbf Z}B$ into $\mathbf Q[H_{\mathbf Q}]\otimes_{\mathbf Q}\mathbf Q[H_{\mathbf Q}]$. The matrix comultiplication of any $f\in I$ is zero in this last ring, since $H_{\mathbf Q}$ is a subgroup; injectivity makes it zero already in $B\otimes B$. Inversion and the identity similarly kill $I$, with values in $B$ and $\mathbf Z$. Thus the matrix operations descend to $\mathcal C$ and satisfy the group diagrams, inherited from matrices. This is a flat affine finite-type group scheme: $B$ is a quotient of the finitely generated matrix coordinate ring. The torus and root maps factor through $\mathcal C$, since the pullback of $I$ vanishes rationally and their source rings $\mathbf Z[P]$ and $\mathbf Z[a]$ are torsion-free. Consequently every specified integral word $n_w$ belongs to $\mathcal C(\mathbf Z)$.

source.place: Equation (153), printed p.510; agent coordinate-kernel proof of the closure group law, without any claim about special fibres.

proof.text:
The subgroup theorem [lem-weil-subgroup-finite-free-abelian-group-free] gives bases of $\Lambda\cap W_\lambda$. The weight lattice is finite free by [lem-sfb-root-datum-lattice-embedding] applied to the free root lattice $M=\mathbf Z\Delta$ (all roots have integral simple-root coordinates and coroots take integral values on it), so $\mathbf Z[P]$ is a Laurent polynomial algebra. Choose a rational functional on $V$ positive on $\Delta$ and separating $\Omega$: perturb the functional taking value $1$ on each simple root to avoid the finitely many weight-equality hyperplanes. Clear its denominators on a basis of $P$, obtaining $q:P\to\mathbf Z$. Order the weight blocks by decreasing $q(\lambda)$. The bracket relation implies $D_{\alpha,m}W_\lambda\subseteq W_{\lambda+m\alpha}$, hence
$$t y_\alpha(a)t^{-1}=y_\alpha(\alpha(t)a).$$
The divided-power identity $D_{\alpha,i}D_{\alpha,j}=\binom{i+j}{i}D_{\alpha,i+j}$ gives $y_\alpha(a)y_\alpha(b)=y_\alpha(a+b)$ and inverse $y_\alpha(-a)$. All these identities hold integrally by comparison in torsion-free polynomial matrix rings; no factorial is inverted in a test algebra. The products $p_+,p_-$ are upper and lower block unitriangular, respectively.

source.place: Equation (152), printed p.510; explicit weight, lattice and coefficient calculations.

proof.text: For either sign, [lem-sfb-chevalley-unipotent-polynomial-coordinates] makes $(p_\pm)_F$ a closed immersion for every algebraically closed field $F$. Give its target polynomial ring $\mathbf Z[z_\beta]$ the strictly positive degrees $q(\beta)$, using the cocharacter $q$ for $p_+$ and $-q$ for $p_-$. The coordinate pullback from $\mathbf Z[\operatorname{GL}_\Lambda]$ is graded by conjugation, by step 2; the matrix coordinate ring has the corresponding integer grading. Let $M_d$ be its image in the degree-$d$ part of the target. That part is finite free, because all variable degrees are positive. The quotient $C_d$ is finitely generated, and field surjectivity gives $C_d\otimes\mathbf Q=0$ and $C_d/pC_d=0$ for every prime $p$, by faithful scalar extension to algebraic closures and right exactness of quotient tensor products. Thus $C_d$ is finite, and if nonzero has a quotient of prime order, contradicting $C_d/pC_d=0$. Hence all $C_d=0$ and both integral $p_\pm$ are closed immersions. Write their images $\mathcal U_\pm$.

source.place: Equation (153) and Theorem 23.72, pp.510-511; agent positive-degree argument upgrading field coordinate surjectivity to integral surjectivity.

proof.text:
The weight-character torus is closed in the block diagonal group: restriction of a diagonal entry on the weight-$\lambda$ block is $e^\lambda$, and the corresponding entry of the inverse matrix is $e^{-\lambda}$. Their products generate $\mathbf Z[P]$ since $\mathbf Z\Omega=P$, giving a surjection on coordinate rings. The three closed immersions $\mathcal U_-\subset L$, $\mathcal T\subset D$, $\mathcal U_+\subset U$ give a closed immersion of their product into $L\times D\times U$, since tensor products of surjections are surjective. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-block-gauss-chart] over $\mathbf Z$ to the weight blocks. It follows that
$$j:\mathbf A^N\times\mathcal T\times\mathbf A^N\longrightarrow\operatorname{GL}_\Lambda,\quad(a,t,b)\mapsto p_-(a)t p_+(b)$$
is a closed immersion into the Gauss principal open, hence a quasi-compact immersion. Its source has a polynomial Laurent-polynomial coordinate ring $A_0$ over $\mathbf Z$.

source.place: The matrix Gauss step below (152)-(153), p.510; relative Gauss lemma is used over Z, not the field-only chart.

proof.text: Let $J$ be the kernel of $j_{\mathbf Q}^*$. Over $\overline{\mathbf Q}$, [lem-sfb-chevalley-root-exponential-group] identifies the generated root group $H$ as semisimple and containing the weight torus. The field chart [lem-sfb-chevalley-exponential-big-cell] is open in $H$, which is reductive by [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure], and $H$ is geometrically integral by [lem-sfb-bruhat-longest-cell-charts]. Thus its scheme-theoretic image is all of $H$, so $J\otimes\overline{\mathbf Q}$ is its subgroup ideal. Matrix multiplication, inverse and identity preserve $J$: test this after the faithfully flat field extension $\mathbf Q\subset\overline{\mathbf Q}$, where the assertion has just been proved. Every generator $T_{\mathbf Q},(y_\alpha)_{\mathbf Q}$ factors through $j_{\mathbf Q}$ by setting all other coordinates to zero. Minimality of $H_{\mathbf Q}$ therefore gives $H_{\mathbf Q}\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}(\mathbf Q[\operatorname{GL}]/J)$. The opposite inclusion follows because the product defining $j_{\mathbf Q}$ factors through $H_{\mathbf Q}$. Hence they are equal, and $(H_{\mathbf Q})_{\overline{\mathbf Q}}=H$, in particular the generic fibre is geometrically connected and is smooth by [lem-trf-smooth-fpqc-base-descent] for the flat quasi-compact surjection $\operatorname{Spec}\overline{\mathbf Q}\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Q$.

source.place: Theorem 23.72, pp.510-511, and 21.86, p.452; agent generic-image identification by scalar extension and kernel ideals.

proof.text: Since $A_0$ is torsion-free, the kernel of the integral $j^*$ is the contraction of $J$, which step 5 identifies with $I$. Thus $\mathcal C$ is the scheme-theoretic image of the quasi-compact immersion $j$. Apply [lemma-nagata-immersion-open-in-scheme-image]: its factor $\theta_1$ into $\mathcal C$ is an open immersion. The identity is its point $(0,1,0)$. Left multiplication by $n_w\in\mathcal C(\mathbf Z)$ is an automorphism, with inverse left multiplication by $n_w^{-1}$. Composing it with $\theta_1$ gives exactly the prescribed $\theta_w$, so every one is an open immersion.

source.place: Agent use of quasi-compact immersion/image factorization, Stacks Tag 01RG (lemma-quasi-compact-immersion), for the integral identity chart and its translates.

proof.text: Fix an algebraically closed field $F$ with its map from $\mathbf Z$. Let $H_F$ be the closed subgroup generated by the root matrices over $F$. By [lem-sfb-chevalley-root-exponential-group], it is smooth connected semisimple, contains $T_F$ and has the stipulated root datum. It is a closed subgroup of $\mathcal C_F$, since every generator factors through that closed subgroup by step 1. The base change of $\theta_1$ factors through $H_F$ and has the same formula as the field chart in [lem-sfb-chevalley-exponential-big-cell]. Its image is therefore an open neighbourhood of the identity in $\mathcal C_F$ lying scheme-theoretically in $H_F$. By [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space] and [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base], closed points are dense in every closed subset and have residue field $F$. Translating this open by all points of $H_F(F)$ covers $H_F$: it contains every closed point, and the complement, if nonempty, would contain a closed point in the finite-type $F$-scheme $H_F$. Thus $H_F$ is both open and closed in $\mathcal C_F$. It is connected, so is exactly the identity component, with its reduced structure. By [lem-ag-group-identity-local-dimension], its dimension is the dimension of its local ring at the identity, hence $2N+\operatorname{rank}P$ from the open field chart. The same identity-dimension formula on $H_{\mathbf Q}$, using its rational open chart from step 6, gives the same generic dimension.

source.place: Field-only Theorem 23.72 and the open-cell input, pp.510-511; comparison of the reduced special identity component, not of the entire special fibre.

proof.text: For every prime $p$, apply [lem-sfb-quasi-reductive-special-connectedness] to $\mathcal C\times_{\mathbf Z}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z_{(p)}$. Its coordinate ring is $B\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, with the same finite generators. Tensoring a $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$-module injection with this ring identifies with tensoring it over $\mathbf Z$ with $B$, so flatness follows from step 1. Step 5 gives a smooth geometrically connected generic fibre. Step 7 identifies the reduced geometric special identity component with a semisimple, hence reductive by [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure], group of exactly the generic dimension. All hypotheses of the criterion hold, including at $p=2$ and $p=3$. It follows that $\mathcal C_{\overline{\mathbf F}_p}$ is connected. Its nonempty open-and-closed subgroup $H_{\overline{\mathbf F}_p}$ is therefore the entire scheme: an open immersion with full image is an isomorphism, so no nilpotent structure remains outside $H$. Along with step 5, the same equality holds for any algebraically closed field $F$ over $\mathbf Z$, by scalar extension: the group already identified over $\overline{\mathbf F}_p$ or $\overline{\mathbf Q}$ is geometrically integral by [lem-sfb-bruhat-longest-cell-charts], so remains connected; the open-and-closed argument of step 7 applies again. Thus every geometric fibre of $\mathcal C$ is the field-generated group; this has been proved without interchanging schematic closure and reduction.

source.place: Prasad-Yu, Theorem 1.2(c), pp.1-2, Proposition 4.4(i) and Section 5; local document WANTED. Agent application to each localization Z_(p).

proof.text: Work in $H_F=\mathcal C_F$. Choose a regular cocharacter positive on $R^+$; [lem-sfb-regular-cocharacter-borel-description] supplies the Borel $B$ with these positive roots. Each $y_\alpha$ is a closed additive subgroup, by step 3 applied to its coordinate axis, normalized by $T_F$ with character $\alpha$, and with nonzero tangent vector by [lem-sfb-chevalley-exponential-big-cell]. The uniqueness in [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations] identifies its image with the root subgroup $U_\alpha$. Then [lem-sfb-borel-root-product-coordinates] and [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure] identify $(p_+)_F$ with $R_u(B)$, $(p_-)_F$ with the opposite unipotent radical $U_-$, and the chart image with $U_-B$. This is a right $B$-invariant and left $T_F$-invariant open subset of $H_F$.

source.place: Milne 21.19, 21.32-21.35 and 21.68(a), pp.431-445; field root-subgroup and Borel identification from the existing field results.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-chevalley-integral-rank-one], each specified $n_\delta$ normalizes the torus and acts as $s_\delta$ on its character lattice. By [lem-sfb-weyl-reflection-realization] the normalizer quotient is the root reflection group. Simple reflections generate it: [lem-sfb-root-base-reflection-induction] applied to the predicate that a root is in a signed simple-root orbit proves every root reflection is a conjugate of a simple one. Thus the chosen words $n_w$ represent every element of the actual Weyl group of $H_F$, and have the required action, regardless of choices of reduced words. Set $Q=H_F/B$. By [lem-sfb-flag-torus-fixed-geometry], it is projective with an equivariant projective embedding, and its torus fixed points are precisely $e_w=n_wB$.

source.place: Milne 21.41 and 21.84, pp.437 and 451; specified Chevalley reflection words as representatives, and the fixed-flag description.

proof.text: Let $O\subseteq Q$ be the image of $U_-B$ under the right $B$-torsor $\pi:H_F\to Q$. It is open and $\pi^{-1}(O)=U_-B$: on each torsor trivializing open $V$ of [lem-sfb-bruhat-longest-cell-charts], take the inverse image of $U_-B$ under its section. This is open in $V$ and its inverse image in $V\times B$ is precisely the right-$B$-invariant open $U_-B$. The section preimages agree on overlaps, since the sections differ by right multiplication by $B$. Each $n_wO$ is $T_F$-invariant and contains $e_w$. Their union has closed $T_F$-invariant complement $Z\subseteq Q$. If $z\in Z(F)$, use the cocharacter of [lem-sfb-flag-torus-fixed-geometry] whose fixed locus equals $Q^T$. In its projective embedding write a representative of $z$ as $\sum v_m$ in weight spaces, and let $m_0$ be the least weight with $v_{m_0}\ne0$. The morphism $t\mapsto[\sum t^{m-m_0}v_m]$ extends the orbit to $t=0$, with value $[v_{m_0}]$. This lies in $Z$ since $Z$ is closed, and lies in $Q^T$ by the choice of cocharacter. But every point of $Q^T$ is an $e_w$, already in $n_wO$, a contradiction. By [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space] and [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base], a nonempty closed finite-type $F$-scheme has an $F$-point, so $Z$ is empty. Pulling back to $H_F$ shows that the opens $n_wU_-B$ cover the geometric fibre.

source.place: Milne 21.84 and 21.86, pp.451-452; explicit projective weight-limit argument for the Weyl translates of the identity chart.

proof.text: Any point of $\mathcal C$ lifts to a geometric point of its fibre, by extending its residue field to an algebraic closure. Step 11 puts that point in the base change of some $\theta_w$, so the original point belongs to the image of that open immersion. Hence the $\theta_w$ cover $\mathcal C$. If $R=\varnothing$, the spanning hypothesis gives $V=P=0$. There are no root maps, the torus is the identity group, and the smallest rational subgroup and its integral schematic closure are both $1$. There is only $w=1$, its products are empty, and $\theta_1$ is the identity of $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. This also handles a zero-dimensional representation of the zero Lie algebra.

source.place: Agent assembly from geometric-fibre coverage; empty-root case of the explicit construction.

Shape: one commit; uses = proof_deps; no cycle (the closure misses the item and its parent lem-sfb-chevalley-integral-root-model); no SGA 4 hit under the review_split regex; not superseded, since live and side-live still show the item unsplit. Sources: Milne iAG printed pp.509-511 (152, 153, Thm 23.72, which is field-only with omitted details, and 'Reductive groups over Z'). Prasad-Yu is not in local literature; I read pp.1-2 of the arXiv PDF math/0405381. Their quasi-reductive definition (affine flat, generic fibre smooth connected, (G_kbar)°_red reductive with dim = dim G_K) matches the new DVR node hypothesis by hypothesis. Thm 1.2(c), special fibre connected, has no characteristic restriction. Connected special fibre is equivalent to G_kbar connected for a group scheme with a rational identity. New node lem-sfb-relative-block-gauss-chart: true over any commutative ring by block LDU with Schur complements and Δ_j(ldu) = ∏det d_i. Tested on s=0, s=1, 2x2 explicit factors, the zero ring and nilpotent algebras. It generalizes the field-only lem-sfb-block-gauss-scheme-chart, which cannot give the chart over Z needed in step 4, so it is not a duplicate. Neither new node restates the item. Steps: (1) flat tensor injection twice gives the descent of the Hopf operations; T and y_α factor through C. (2) P is free via the root-datum node with M = ZΔ; conjugation and divided-power identities check. (3) Grading by the q-cocharacter, C_d f.g. with C_d⊗Q = C_d/p = 0, so the integral closed immersion holds. (4) T is closed in D because ZΩ = P; the relative Gauss chart over Z gives a quasi-compact immersion. (5) H = K by the root-exponential and big-cell nodes, which are open and geometrically integral; J⊗Qbar = I(H), so V(J) = H_Q; smoothness descends along fpqc. (6) ker j^* = J∩Z[GL] = I and Nagata gives the open immersion θ_1; θ_w follow by translation by n_w in C(Z). (7) Translates of the open chart cover H_F, which is therefore open and closed in C_F; identity-local dimension gives 2N + rk P on both fibres. (8) The DVR criterion over Z_(p) makes C_Fpbar connected, equal to H, and extends to other algebraically closed F by scalar extension. (9) U_α by uniqueness; the chart image is U_-B. (10) n_δ represents s_δ; simple reflections generate; fixed points are n_wB. (11) Torsor-section openness and a λ-limit into Q^T contradict a nonempty complement. (12) Geometric points give coverage; R=∅ gives C = Spec Z. I also checked SL2/Z: the two charts are where the (1,1) or the (2,1) entry is a unit. Batch-5 flags: lem-trf-flat-tensor-preserves-injection and lem-trf-smooth-fpqc-base-descent (direct cites), and the closures through fppf-covering-base-change, smooth-composition, fg-torsionfree-group-free and split-lattice-torus-projection, are all generic Mathlib-level algebra or geometry, not the trace formula or Poincaré duality or their proofs. I accept the tool_use lem-ag-group-identity-local-dimension. No fixes.

lean.note: All helper definitions belong to the explicit closure-and-chart construction of this node. The rational subgroup ideal is constructed as the vanishing ideal of its generated rational points; density of the split torus and affine line over Q identifies it with the smallest closed subgroup scheme. Z and Q are canonically universe lifted. The existential matrix basis and polynomial maps are completely characterized by their stated formulas on all algebra-valued points.
